<!-- docs-drift-check -->
### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **5** package(s): `@objectstack/core`, `@objectstack/lint`, `@objectstack/metadata-core`, `@objectstack/metadata-protocol`, `@objectstack/objectql`, touching **84** documentable anchor(s). ⚠️ **3** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/core/src/index.ts`, `packages/metadata-core/src/index.ts`, `packages/objectql/src/index.ts`), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

**39** hand-written doc(s) name something this change touched — list omitted above 15 rows. Re-derive on the tree named below: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 90cea476dedee4bb2586f60b4f469bba67904cf3`.

⛔ **15** release-owned page(s) also affected — read-only, see AGENTS.md Documentation Guardrails.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **3** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/core/src/index.ts`, `packages/metadata-core/src/index.ts`, `packages/objectql/src/index.ts`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- **1** anchor(s) matched too much of the corpus to be a work list: `ObjectQL (symbol, 80 pages)`
- **17** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **65** of **231** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **166** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **166**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **107** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **55** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 90cea476dedee4bb2586f60b4f469bba67904cf3` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `418187dcf97b0cc2d6a73d830ce42d52828c1428` — the merge of head `c1c1536725037e9ad2473b8fa7f07ad8853b584b` into base `90cea476dedee4bb2586f60b4f469bba67904cf3`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 418187dcf97b0cc2d6a73d830ce42d52828c1428 && git checkout 418187dcf97b0cc2d6a73d830ce42d52828c1428
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 90cea476dedee4bb2586f60b4f469bba67904cf3 c1c1536725037e9ad2473b8fa7f07ad8853b584b && git checkout -B drift-repro 90cea476dedee4bb2586f60b4f469bba67904cf3 && git merge --no-ff c1c1536725037e9ad2473b8fa7f07ad8853b584b

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 90cea476dedee4bb2586f60b4f469bba67904cf3
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 90cea476dedee4bb2586f60b4f469bba67904cf3` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

epic:#31527#1 · os-steve · session_01ADHkmP7o3uDTti21wLTfPf

**Epic acceptance review: R2 #31716, head e4cadc74 · 2026-11-09T00:38Z**

Verdict: **CHANGES REQUIRED.** There are two items, both of the "do not narrow an answer that works today" kind (red line 3 (b)). The move itself is accepted.

**Accepted:**
- The pure rule `resolvePackageScopedHolders` in `@objectstack/core`, over a supplied holder source and closure.
- The one walk in `@objectstack/metadata-core` (`packageResolutionClosure` / `packageDependencyClosure` / `resolvePackageClosure` / `widenPairClosureToAppMembers`), re-exported under the old names by lint, metadata-protocol and objectql, with identity pins that prove there is no second closure.
- `check:lean-entry-closure` is green and `ADMITTED_PACKAGES` is unchanged.
- `resolvePackageScopedName` is now the registry adapter with the same signature, and R's tests are untouched.
- The engine's `functionHolders` sits beside the bare map, with `resolveFunction` untouched and no reader wired.
- The bundle-addition holder rule for ambiguity counting is accepted. It covers both arms: a dependent holding the base's member stays a holder, and so does a package that does not declare the holder (both ablated red).

**Item 1: a package caller's bare read of its own added member must not become not-found.**
- Before this PR, R counts dependent D, which adds `fr` to B's bundle, as a holder. So D's bare read of `fr` is answered at step 1 (`own`) by D's member.
- At head, `packageHolders` is filtered, so `holders.includes(D)` fails, step 2 picks B, and B ships no `fr`: not-found.
- That narrows an answer that works on main. Required: use the filtered holder set only for counting ambiguity. Step 1 still asks whether the caller holds the name, unfiltered, and answers with its own item.
- Pin both directions with a test that is red without the fix: D reading `fr` gets D's member; D reading `en` (B's only) is unchanged from main.
- The member-grain improvement (reading `en` falling back to B) stays the later R amendment you named.

**Item 2: an owner-less function registration is the platform's, not the environment's item.**
- `resolvePackageScopedFunction` reads `null` as the environment's own item. For a package caller whose only holder is owner-less, that ends at step 3 as `outside-closure`, which is the D3 (a) refusal.
- Today the bare map answers that reference. An owner-less `engine.registerFunction` is code a plugin or host registers, never an item authored in the environment (D1 bucket 4 is authored metadata).
- **Ruling:** treat it like `sys` (D2), reachable from every caller's closure. That means: own package first; then the unique holder among closure plus owner-less; two or more of those is `ambiguous-in-closure`, naming each; a caller with no package keeps the environment-wide order.
- Pin it with a test: a package caller with only an owner-less holder resolves to it, and an owner-less holder next to a closure holder refuses naming both. It must be red without the fix.
- `ENGINE_FUNCTION_TYPE` already sidesteps the platform-requested arm, so the change stays in the function adapter's holder source.

**Open questions:**
- *Fixes vs Part of:* `Fixes #31716` plus `Part of #31527`.
- *New public names* (`resolvePackageScopedHolders`, `PackageScopedHolderSource`, `packageScopedHolderSource`, `resolvePackageScopedFunction`, `ObjectQL#functionHoldersOf`): accepted, as the seat's call.
- *Owner-less = environment:* ruled the other way, as above.
- *Member-grain:* deferred to the later R amendment, as above, once Item 1 keeps today's answer.

This surface is not governed. Once both items are in and CI is green, I accept and land it, then release E2, E3, E6, E8 and E5's email half.

epic:#31527#1 · os-steve · session_01ADHkmP7o3uDTti21wLTfPf

**Epic acceptance re-review: R2 #31716, head 15d685cf · 2026-11-09T01:59Z**

All four rulings are in and pinned red without the fix: the own holding at step 1, the platform holder, the `__runtime__` caller, and the residual closure. Two things remain before I accept it.

**1. A caller with no package: the platform must not outrank a package holder (red line 2).**
- `resolveEnvironmentWide` answers environment item → `platformItem` → unique package holder. So an owner-less registration and package P's function of the same name resolve to the platform without a word. That is a pick.
- D3, for a caller with no package, is the environment's own item, else the unique holder, else a refusal. The platform is one more holder there, as `sys` packages are; it does not get its own step ahead of the packages.
- Required: after the environment item, count the platform holder with the package holders. Exactly one answers. Two or more refuse with `ambiguous-in-environment`, naming each, the platform included.
- Pin: owner-less plus P, with a caller that names no package, refuses naming both. Owner-less alone still answers.
- The package-caller order you built (own → unique among closure plus platform) is right as it stands.

**2. The save-door effect for residual owners needs its count.**
- A write stamped with a residual owner's id used to narrow nothing. It is now judged against the owner's declared closure.
- That follows from N1's ruling (declared closure only) and is the root fix, but it is a narrowing at the save door, so red line 3 needs its number.
- Measure the first-party residual owners whose writes would now be refused: the repo's example and dogfood stacks, plus HotCRM if you can reach it. Put the count on the `Narrowing:` line.
- At 0, it lands as declared. Above 0, stop and tell me before landing.

**Accepted this round:**
- the own holding kept at step 1, in both storage shapes;
- the platform holder with kind and step `platform` for a package caller;
- `RUNTIME_COMPATIBILITY_PACKAGE_ID`, normalized on the caller side only (an item stamped `__runtime__` stays a holder);
- the residual dependency map with no package record, read by the one walk;
- no N1 widening and no Q1 sealed-set arm;
- the new public names.

Send me the head with both changes and I will accept it and land it myself (the epic seat's own card; not a governed surface).
